summary: Backend-only testing for OpsCore. Wrote pytest suite (25 tests) covering JWT auth, Projects/Tasks/Notes CRUD, Dashboard summary, Analytics overview (14 daily + 7x24 heatmap), Team invites (graceful no-RESEND fallback), Notifications (overdue/due_soon/blocked), Focus sessions (actual_minutes increment), and all 6 AI endpoints with REAL Claude Sonnet 4.5 calls (chat multi-turn, conversations list/get, rewrite, breakdown w/ subtask persistence, summarize-project, prioritize). All 25 tests PASS. Authentication blocks unauthorized access (401), no _id/password_hash leakage, email lowercasing verified.

minor.issue: Odd code pattern: doc['_id']=None; doc.pop('_id') (lines 418-419). Works but unnecessary; should just pop existing key. Cosmetic only.

DELETE /api/projects/{pid} only deletes when user is owner (owner_id match), but if a non-owner member calls it, request returns {ok:true} silently with no 403/404. Consider returning 403 if not owner.
Uses 'status_filter' query param instead of more idiomatic 'status'. Frontend must use ?status_filter=... matching this. Not a bug, just naming.
Returns 403 (FastAPI HTTPBearer default) instead of 401 when Authorization header is absent. With invalid token it correctly returns 401. Minor inconsistency.

action_items: Optional: return 403 from DELETE /projects/{pid} when caller is not owner (currently silent no-op)
Optional: align /auth/me to return 401 (not 403) when no Authorization header
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 861 lines — should be split into routers (auth, projects, tasks, notes, ai, analytics) before next feature wave.

AI multi-turn history is reconstructed into the user message string (history_str). LlmChat session_id alone could maintain context server-side; current approach doubles tokens. Functional, but suboptimal.

ai/breakdown and ai/prioritize parse JSON via find('{')/rfind('}'). If Claude returns mixed text+JSON, parsing may fail silently — has a fallback to empty list which is handled, but could log a warning.
Indexes: no MongoDB indexes defined for users.email, tasks.owner_id, projects.members, etc. Will degrade at scale.
JWT_SECRET fallback ('dev-secret') in code allows insecure deployment if env missing. Consider requiring it.
Token revocation/blacklist not implemented — logout is client-side only.
seed_data_creation: Tests create TEST_-prefixed projects/tasks/notes/invites and clean up after themselves. Founder account leaves a handful of AI conversation rows + invites — acceptable for demo data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 25 backend tests in /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py pass against external URL. AI tests use real Claude (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) via EMERGENT_LLM_KEY and take ~30s total. RESEND_API_KEY is intentionally blank — /team/invite returns emailed=false with invite_url. Frontend not tested (per request).
rca_of_the_issue: n/a — no bugs found that block functionality. All 14 module endpoints listed in the review request return expected responses.
